_meta.note: Hand-authored Latin American catalog centred on Mexico City, with Guadalajara, Monterrey, Buenos Aires, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Lima, Bogotá, Havana, Santiago and Montevideo. Shaped like Qloo Insights entities plus a `_syn` block used for scoring and stripped before serving. Entity ids are fake. Not Qloo data.

properties.short_description: The idol of Mexico's Golden Age: 'Amorcito corazón', 'Cien años', 'Las mañanitas', and the star of Nosotros los pobres.
'El Charro Cantor': 'México lindo y querido', 'Ay, Jalisco, no te rajes', the operatic voice of the ranchera film.
The king of bolero ranchero: 'Sombras', 'Payaso', 'En mi viejo San Juan'.
Wrote 'El Rey', 'Caminos de Guanajuato', 'Si nos dejan' and hundreds more of the songs Mexico sings.
'Lola la Grande': 'Cucurrucucú paloma', 'Paloma negra', the great voice of ranchera on stage and screen.
The composer at the piano: 'Granada', 'Solamente una vez', 'María bonita', 'Veracruz'.
The trío romántico with the requinto guitar: 'Bésame mucho', 'Sin ti', 'Rayito de luna'.
'El Charro de México': corridos and rancheras, and more than a hundred films on horseback.
'Volver, volver' (1972), 'El Rey', 'Mujeres divinas': the charro cantor of the next generation.

akas.value: El Rey de la Música Ranchera

properties.short_description: 'No tengo dinero' (1971), 'Amor eterno', 'Querida': the Divo de Juárez, writing hits from the start of the 1970s.
'El Príncipe de la Canción': 'La nave del olvido' (1970), 'El triste', 'Gavilán o paloma'.
'Somos novios', 'Contigo aprendí', 'Esta tarde vi llover': the bolero's great composer from Yucatán.
The ranchera singer in a poncho, with a tequila on the piano: 'Macorina', 'La llorona', 'Piensa en mí'.
properties.place_of_birth: San Joaquín de Flores, Costa Rica

properties.short_description: 'La Grandota de Camargo': rancheras in the big voice, and films alongside Antonio Aguilar.
'El Lujo de México': boleros from Guadalajara, 'Luz y sombra', 'Por amor'.
The Mexico City dance orchestra since 1955: 'La boa', 'Perfume de gardenias', every quinceañera's band.
'El Ídolo de Matamoros': tropical cumbia with electric guitars, 'Mi Matamoros querido', 'Lamento de amor'.
The norteño band from Sinaloa, in California since 1968: 'Contrabando y traición' (1972), 'La puerta negra'.
'La Guarachera de Cuba': with the Sonora Matancera in Havana, then the queen of salsa in New York, 'La vida es un carnaval'.
'El Bárbaro del Ritmo': the Cuban bandleader of 'Cómo fue', 'Bonito y sabroso', 'Santa Isabel de las Lajas'.
properties.place_of_birth: Santa Isabel de las Lajas, Cuba

properties.short_description: The voice of tango: 'Por una cabeza', 'Mi Buenos Aires querido', 'Volver'. He sings better every day, they say.
'Pichuco', the bandoneón of Buenos Aires: 'Sur', 'Garúa', the great orchestra of the tango's golden decade.
'Libertango', 'Adiós Nonino': the bandoneón that pulled tango into the concert hall.
'La Negra', the voice of nueva canción: 'Gracias a la vida', 'Alfonsina y el mar', 'Sólo le pido a Dios'.
'Sandro de América': 'Rosa, Rosa' (1969), 'Penumbras', the first Latin rock idol to fill Madison Square Garden.
'La felicidad', 'Yo tengo fe': the Club del Clan idol who became the Rey of Argentine pop and film.
'Celia', 'Cómo te extraño mi amor', 'Esa pared': the Argentine balladeer who became a Mexican favourite.
The Chilean band of 'Y volveré' and 'Murió la flor': boleros over electric organ, a hit across the continent.
'El Ruiseñor de América': 'Nuestro juramento', 'Fatalidad', the Ecuadorian voice of the bolero and the pasillo.
'Gracias a la vida', 'Volver a los 17': the folklorist who gathered Chile's songs and wrote its best.
'La flor de la canela', 'Fina estampa': Lima's criollo waltzes written for the city she walked.
'O Rei' of Brazilian pop: the Jovem Guarda years, then 'Detalhes', 'Amigo', 'Emoções'.
properties.place_of_birth: Cachoeiro de Itapemirim, Espírito Santo, Brazil

properties.short_description: 'Garota de Ipanema', 'Desafinado', 'Corcovado': bossa nova's composer, at the piano in Rio.
'Águas de março' with Tom Jobim, 'Como nossos pais', 'O bêbado e a equilibrista': the voice of MPB.
The whispering guitar of 'Chega de saudade' (1958) that started bossa nova.
'A banda' (1966), 'Construção', 'Apesar de você': songs that slipped past the censors.
'A Voz de Veludo': boleros and sambas-canção, 'A Volta do Boêmio', 'Fica comigo esta noite'.
